functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Only two-joint muscle of the adductor group; long thin strap shape and long fascicles suit its dual hip-adduction/knee-flexion role. Frequently harvested as a tendon graft (e.g. ACL reconstruction, typically combined with semitendinosus as an STG graft), and generally considered to carry comparatively low donor-site morbidity given its functional redundancy with the other adductors and hamstrings -- though some studies debate whether adding gracilis to a semitendinosus-only graft meaningfully increases donor-site morbidity (e.g. residual knee-flexion deficits), so "no functional cost at all" would overstate the case (softened after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: the line connecting the centre of the patella and the medial femoral condyle
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Attributed to Won et al. Note the 100% end is a LINE, not a point, so the reference line is drawn to it perpendicularly rather than to a single landmark.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the proximal third of the medial thigh, with the limb supine and the hip abducted, externally rotated and semi-flexed and the knee semi-flexed.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Most superficial of the medial group, lying over two deeper muscle masses which sit on the femoral cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The non-standard limb position is required to bring the muscle under the probe. Reducing gracilis spasticity improves hip abduction and knee extension, reduces scissoring, and eases hygiene, seating and orthosis tolerance; in cerebral palsy it may also help prevent hip dislocation.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
